meru-ukraine-defense-chief-purge:
A country at war fired its defense minister and, six days later, replaced its top general as well.
That happened in Ukraine on July 15 and July 21.

@@REF@@Ukraine's reformist defense minister is out after six months, and earlier his audit exposed $7.2 billion in defense overspending (Euromaidan Press, 2026-07-15)|https://euromaidanpress.com/2026/07/15/ukraines-reformist-defense-minister-is-out-after-six-months-earlier-his-audit-exposed-7-2-billion-in-defense-overspending/|https://euromaidanpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/photo_2026-04-15_13-36-04.jpg

The piece lays out what Mykhailo Fedorov did in six months on the job.
An internal audit of the ministry turned up $7.2 billion of overspending, weapons procurement moved to open tenders, and ministry staff were put through polygraph tests.
Meru puts the overspending at $6.7 billion, a slightly different count of the same audit.

Most coverage framed the shake-up as a clash of doctrine, a 35-year-old minister betting on drones against a 60-year-old general raised on infantry warfare.
That is not where the break actually ran.

## Why the two became rivals rather than boss and subordinate

After losing Crimea in 2014, Ukraine adopted NATO-style civilian control, putting a civilian defense minister in charge of supervising the military.
On the org chart the minister now sat above the commander-in-chief.

The reporting line was left as it was.
Both men kept reporting directly to the president and taking their orders from him.

Move it into a company and it reads clearly.
You put the head of investments in charge of supervising the head of trading, then have the chief executive grade both of them personally.
To the head of trading, the head of investments is not a boss. He is a competitor.

## Why the arrangement held for twelve years

Where the boundaries of authority are vague, a person usually fills the gap.
Andriy Yermak, the president's chief of staff, was that person.
When the minister and the general collided, the president's office settled it, and when parliament balked, Yermak settled that.

In November 2025 Yermak resigned over a corruption scandal in the energy sector.
His successor could not do the same work, and the president's office lost its grip on parliament.
In a chamber where 226 votes are a majority, the bloc that reliably followed the president shrank from about 250 members to about 130.

A structure held up by a person rather than by rules shows its blueprint the moment that person leaves.

## Why 16% is the number that matters

What Fedorov touched was procurement.
He moved 155mm artillery shells to competitive tender, and the price came down 16%.

@@REF@@Procurement of 155-mm ammunition for the armed forces via tender saved 16% of allocated funds (Militarnyi, 2026-05-21)|https://militarnyi.com/en/news/procurement-of-155-mm-ammunition-ukraine/|https://militarnyi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/155-mm-snaryad-1-1024x576.jpg

That report carries the figure Fedorov gave journalists himself in May.
Buying the same shells in the same quantity for 16% less does not mean the shells got cheaper.
It means someone had been taking that 16% off the top.

So the reform saved budget and cut off an income stream in the same motion.

## Why a capable minister becomes dangerous

@@CMP@@The common reading|A young drone-first minister collided with an old infantry general, and the president sided with the army|Meru's reading|In a system with no clear boundary of authority, a minister pushing reform cannot be checked by legal means, so he is removed instead

Same dismissal. One side sees a fight over doctrine, the other sees an empty box in the institutional design.

Protests began on July 16, the day after the dismissal.
Veterans and serving soldiers led them, and they spread to more than sixteen cities.
On July 21 President Zelenskyy met the demand, dismissed Syrskyi and appointed 43-year-old Mykhailo Drapatyi in his place.

@@REF@@Ukraine overhauls its military top brass for the fight against Russia (NPR, 2026-07-21)|https://www.npr.org/2026/07/21/g-s1-134849/ukraine-military-chief-fired-protests|https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/dims3/default/strip/false/crop/5747x3233+0+300/resize/1400/quality/85/format/jpeg/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F7a%2F6c%2F406b76d44540921843b4d9c347bc%2Fap26202419840471.jpg

In that report Syrskyi points to 743 square kilometers retaken this year as his record, and Fedorov calls Drapatyi a voice for change.
The minister's chair is still empty, the confirmation vote delayed by the protests.

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Was this a chain of command being tidied up, or a reform being rolled back.

If open tenders widen to drone procurement under Drapatyi and a new minister is confirmed, the first reading holds.
If procurement slides back behind closed doors and the ministry stays without a minister, this was the point where the reform stopped.

Where institutions work, a capable minister is an asset to the state.
Where they do not, there is no legal way to check him, and a capable minister turns into a threat.
jukan-korea-deleveraging-90-percent-jpmo:
Most of the Korean stock that was bought with borrowed money has already been sold, according to a note out this week.
JPMorgan wrote on July 29 that leveraged ETFs in the Korean market have largely been liquidated and estimated that hedge fund deleveraging is about 90% complete.

@@REF@@Samsung and SK Hynix may rebound as South Korea's leveraged ETF liquidation wave nears its end, JPMorgan says (TradingKey, 2026-07-29)|https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/more/262061488-jpmorgan-wave-liquidations-leveraged-etfs-south-korea-nearing-end-samsung-sk-hynix-rebound-opportunity-tradingkey|https://resource.tradingkey.com/uploads/20260602/samsung-11-eac34728e17f43bb932b61ca59da911f.jpg

The English write-up of that note carries the direction but not the 90% figure.
What it does say is that the liquidation wave is nearing its end, and that this correction came out of capital flows rather than anything breaking inside the businesses.

On the same day the Kospi fell 8.2% to 5,531.56 during Seoul trading, with circuit breakers firing for a second straight session.
The selling that had to happen was nearly finished, and the drop got bigger anyway.

## What deleveraging is, and why it hits this hard

Unwinding a position bought with borrowed money is called deleveraging.
When prices fall, the borrower runs short of collateral and has to sell, and that selling pushes prices lower, which forces the next sale.

This kind of selling does not look at whether a company is good or bad.
The size of the position decides what gets sold, so strong results get dumped alongside weak ones.

That is why counting how much of this supply is left has become the most common piece of arithmetic in the Korean market right now.

## The pile really did shrink

@@CHK@@Leveraged ETF assets (end-June)|$50bn|As of July 21|$26bn|JPMorgan's normal level|$18bn|Deleveraging complete (July 21)|75%|Deleveraging complete (July 29)|about 90%|Kospi, July 29 session|-8.2%@@The liquidation genuinely progressed. Completion went from 75% to 90% in eight days, and the index still fell more than 8% that day. Supply shrinking and prices stabilizing are not the same story.@@JPMorgan note of 2026-07-21 as reported by BigGo Finance · Seoul session index of 2026-07-29 as reported by AP

The July 21 note counted it this way.
Money sitting in these leveraged ETFs had fallen from $50 billion at the end of June to $26 billion, and $18 billion was the level JPMorgan considered normal.
Three quarters of that distance had been covered, and eight days later the figure was 90%.

## So why did it fall further

Forced liquidation was not the only seller that day.

SK Hynix dropped as much as 15% in a session, and roughly a quarter of its market value went in two days.
This is the company that had reported a sixfold jump in quarterly profit the day before.
In the same release it said capital spending would rise to at least $31 billion.

@@REF@@Korean stocks see record wave of trading halts on chip selloff (Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-29)|https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/korean-stocks-see-record-wave-040901347.html|https://s.yimg.com/cv/apiv2/cv/apiv2/social/images/yahoo-finance-default-logo.png

That report counts nine of the fifteen circuit breakers since 2000 as having happened this year.
It also quotes a market voice giving the reason for selling as the capex line, not the profit line.
The news that the company earned more and the news that it will spend more landed on the same day, and the market looked at the second one.

@@CMP@@JPMorgan's reading|The selling that has to happen is nearly done. What is left is stock supported by earnings|The reading from that session|As forced selling winds down, selling based on a judgment about earnings is starting

Same completion percentage, and one side sees the end of the selling while the other sees a change in who is doing it.

## One pile that has not been counted

From July 31, buying a single-stock leveraged ETF in Korea requires 30 million won of cash sitting in the account.
Money from selling shares counts only two days later, once settlement completes.

Averaging down as prices fall gets much harder, and whatever selling that rule produces is not inside the 90% JPMorgan counted.

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Is the selling now the tail of the liquidation, or a new wave based on a view of earnings.

If the declines stop after the July 31 rule takes effect, JPMorgan's reading holds and leverage was the last thing shaking this market.
If they continue after that, the seller has already changed, and counting completion percentages stops meaning anything.

Selling created by borrowed money has an end. Once the debt is repaid there is nothing left to sell.
Selling created by a judgment has no such end.
jukan-korea-leverage-etf-professional-on:
South Korea's financial regulator is weighing a rule that would let only professional investors buy the 2x ETFs that track a single stock such as Samsung Electronics or SK hynix.
Financial Services Commission chairman Lee Eok-won said so himself, answering questions at a July 29 National Assembly committee session.

@@REF@@FSC Chief Weighs Limiting Single-Stock Leverage to Professional Investors (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-07-29)|https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/07/29/fsc-chief-weighs-limiting-single-stock-leverage-to|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/07/29/rcv.NEWS1.NEWS1.20260729.2026-07-29T102835_1008030758_POLITICS_I_P1.jpg

At the same briefing he raised a second idea: cutting the 2x multiple itself.
Two times is too much right now, he said, and dialing it back would help calm the swings.

## What does it take to be a professional investor

Professional investor is a status the Capital Markets Act grants on the basis of holdings and income.
The name sounds like it asks about your job.
What it actually looks at is money.

The base requirement is a month-end average balance above 50 million won, held for at least one year out of the past five.
On top of that you need one of three things: annual income of 100 million won (150 million for a married couple), net worth of 500 million won excluding the home you live in, or a year in a licensed profession such as accountant or lawyer.

@@CHK@@Month-end average balance|over 50m won|Annual income|over 100m won|Net worth (ex-residence)|over 500m won@@The first box is mandatory; the other two are alternatives, and you only need one of them. Unlike the 30 million won cash deposit taking effect July 31, this is not a bar you clear by depositing more money.@@Checked 2026-07-29 · individual professional investor registration criteria under the Capital Markets Act enforcement decree

So limiting the product to professional investors is not raising a bar.
It is changing who is allowed through the door.

## Then where does the money go

The product existed in Hong Kong first.
A domestic rule caps any single holding in an ETF at 30 percent, which made a single-stock 2x fund impossible to launch at home, and the Hong Kong version took the market in the meantime.

The SK hynix 2x fund listed by Hong Kong manager CSOP Asset Management held 8.65 billion dollars in net assets at the end of May, 8.5 percent of Hong Kong's entire ETF market.
Korean investors held 184.6 million dollars of it, the largest single foreign security held in Hong Kong custody by Korean residents.
Seoul Economic Daily's English edition counted the same fund at 5.37778 billion dollars in net assets in early May, with Korean investors holding 172.11 million dollars of it.
Those figures are dated nearly a month earlier, which is where the gap comes from.

@@REF@@SK hynix Leveraged ETF Tops Global Single-Stock Rankings, Beats Tesla 2x (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-05-08)|https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/05/08/sk-hynix-leveraged-etf-tops-global-single-stock-rankings|https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/05/08/rcv.YNA.20260508.PYH2026050813330001300_P1.jpg

The Hong Kong fund sits outside the FSC's jurisdiction.
If the eligibility test lands on the domestic product alone, retail investors are left with one place to go, and it is the place the regulator cannot reach.

## A separate rule is already dated

From July 31, buying these products requires a cash deposit of 30 million won, up from 10 million.
Only cash counts, and pledging stocks or bonds does not.

That measure was set before this month's slide.
Industry voices at the time reportedly said that moving the start date up by a few days was hard to call a decisive response.
Then came a session in which SK hynix fell 9.6 percent in a day and 58 percent from its high for the year.

## So what settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Is taking retail out of this product protection, or is it a push toward the place supervision cannot follow.

If domestic net assets shrink after the rule lands and Korean holdings of the Hong Kong fund shrink alongside them, protection is the right reading.
If only the domestic side shrinks while Hong Kong grows, the risk was not removed.
It was moved off the ledger.

Cutting the multiple is a different matter.
Changing the leverage on a fund already sold requires a beneficiaries' meeting and the consent of existing holders, as the chairman noted himself.

An eligibility test only stops new buyers.
A multiple change reshapes the payoff for people already holding.

Which of the two arrives first is what decides what this rule actually is.

jukan-skhynix-hbm-2027-lta-price-cap:
SK hynix is negotiating the volumes and prices of the HBM it will sell in 2027 with its major customers right now.
The answer came in the Q&A that followed its second-quarter results on the 28th.

The answer itself was short, that talks are going smoothly. The more useful part came next.
The long-term supply agreements already signed are not contracts that nail a price down to one number.

## Does HBM follow DRAM prices?

The company said conventional DRAM average selling prices rose about 30% from the previous quarter, and NAND rose by the mid-50s in percentage terms.
So the question was whether HBM prices simply ride along.

The answer was that it does not work that way.
Building one HBM stack eats more wafers than plain DRAM of the same capacity, and adds the TSV step that drills through stacked dies to connect them, plus extra packaging.
So prices are set customer by customer, weighing not only conventional DRAM pricing and supply and demand but the resources and the opportunity cost that go into HBM.

Opportunity cost here means the money the same production line would have earned making something else.
When DRAM prices jump, what the company gives up to make HBM instead grows too, and so does its ground for charging more.

The stacking and the through-silicon connections are what push its wafer consumption up.|Smial · FAL 1.3|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DDR5_SDRAM_(with_scale)_IMGP6298_smial_wp.jpg

## Why did July read it the other way?

On 13 July SK hynix shares in Seoul fell 15.4% in one session, the steepest single-day drop in company history.
The reason the market gave that day was these very contracts.
If a price is fixed for several years, the reading went, a spot rally passes the seller by.

Korea Investment & Securities cut its second-quarter operating profit estimate to 60.4 trillion won, about 8% below the 65 trillion won consensus.
The reported figure came in at 60.54 trillion won.
The estimate was almost exactly right, which means the market already knew.

@@REF@@SK hynix posts worst Seoul session on record as HBM contracts are said to limit earnings upside (Tech Times, 2026-07-13)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/320352/20260713/sk-hynix-posts-worst-seoul-session-record-hbm-contracts-limit-earnings-upside.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/465462/hbm.jpg

## What does no cap mean?

On 2 July the Taiwanese research house TrendForce reported that SK hynix had removed the price cap from its long-term agreements.
Spot increases can pass straight through into contract pricing under that structure.
Micron, by contrast, is said to keep both a ceiling and a floor pegged to second-quarter market levels.

The contract terms the company described this week point the same way.
It has closed agreements with about 10 customers including its key accounts, terms run around five years, and deposits are built in so customers stay committed.
What is locked is volume and duration. Price was left open.

@@REF@@SK hynix reportedly removes price cap in memory long-term agreements, diverging from Micron (TrendForce, 2026-07-02)|https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/07/02/news-sk-hynix-reportedly-removes-price-cap-in-memory-long-term-agreements-diverging-from-micron/|https://img.trendforce.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/02104949/SK-hynix-booth-2-624x351.jpg

@@CMP@@July's reading|Multi-year contracts fix the price, so however far memory prices run, SK hynix cannot collect it.|The structure the company and the trade press describe|What the contracts lock is volume and duration. Prices vary by customer and product, and the ceiling is reported to be gone.
The same contract splits readers depending on whether they see it as a lock on price or a lock on volume.

## So what settles it?

It comes down to one question.
Are these contracts a cage around the company's prices, or only around its volumes?

If they cage prices, the gap between DRAM spot prices and SK hynix's own average selling price should keep widening from the third quarter on.
If they cage only volumes, contract prices should follow the spot rally with a lag and that gap should close.

The fact that 2027 volumes and prices are being negotiated right now is half the answer already.
A company that had fixed prices for years would have nothing to renegotiate each year.
The removal of the price cap, though, is trade reporting rather than something the company has confirmed itself, so the next quarter's average selling price is the number to watch alongside it.
meru-kumamoto-hinagu-fault-week-of-watch:
A day after the quake, TSMC's Japan fab, JASM, began returning to normal operation in stages.
TSMC said its employees were safe and the fab structure was unaffected by the quake, and with that confirmed, production is being brought back step by step,
while the detailed equipment inspection and damage assessment are still under way.
The construction site of the second fab next door was not affected either, though part of the work was paused over possible aftershocks.

@@REF@@Employees safe, Kumamoto fab structure unaffected by earthquake: TSMC (Focus Taiwan, 2026-07-29)|https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202607290005|https://imgcdn.cna.com.tw/Eng/WebEngPhotos/1024/2026/20260729/1024x696_527953569342.jpg

Japan's Meteorological Agency, meanwhile, asked for about a week of caution against another quake of this size.
Seismic activity is still elevated, and three more tremors have already been strong enough to shake objects off shelves, a lower 5 on Japan's intensity scale.

@@REF@@Kumamoto hit by intensity 7, activity still elevated, one week of caution urged (NHK, 2026-07-29)|https://news.web.nhk/newsweb/na/na-k10015189251000|https://imgu.web.nhk/news/u/news/html/20260729/K10015189251_2607290408_0729040929_01_02.jpg

## Why one week specifically

Ten years ago in this same Kumamoto, a strong quake at intensity 7 came first.
People took it for the mainshock.
Two days later a larger one, the real mainshock, hit.

The first tremor had not been the main event but the leading edge of a bigger one, what seismologists call a foreshock.
That is why the agency says this quake looks like the 2016 sequence.

## Where this quake came from

Most earthquakes happen where one slab of the earth's crust grinds under another.
That boundary is called a subduction zone, and the very large quakes tend to originate there.

This one did not. It came from a crack inside Kyushu itself.
A crack that can move again is called an active fault, and the one that moved here appears to be the Hinagu fault zone.

@@REF@@The Kumamoto earthquake (M7.1) of July 28, 2026 (Japan Society for Active Fault Studies, 2026-07-28)|https://jsaf.info/jishin/2026/07/20260728202045.html

The Philippine Sea plate slides under the Eurasian plate here at four to six centimeters a year, loading that fault for centuries.
Like a balloon that keeps taking air until it bursts, a fault that has been holding finally slips all at once, and that slip is the earthquake.

This epicenter sits about 20 kilometers south of the 2016 epicenter.
If the 2016 quake released the stress stored in the northern stretch of the fault, this one appears to have released the southern stretch.

## What happened outside the fab

Twenty-eight sections of stone wall collapsed at Kumamoto Castle.
Ten people are unaccounted for after a gas leak at an Aeon mall.
At a paper plant in Yatsushiro, two people were found in cardiac arrest and nine are missing.

Kikuyo Town holds JASM's two fabs along with Sony and Fujifilm facilities inside the same 20-kilometer radius.
One plant holding up is not the same as the region holding up.

## So what actually settles this

It comes down to one question.
Was this the end of it, or the leading edge of something larger the way 2016 was.

If no bigger quake arrives within the week and the aftershocks fade, JASM's staged restart holds.
If another quake of this size or larger hits, everything resets: the building checks that looked finished, the detailed equipment inspection, the restart schedule.

When a fab stops and starts repeatedly, the loss does not scale with downtime alone.
Each restart drags the inspection and requalification steps along with it again.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics is raising prices on certain MLCC products by 30% for shipments made on or after August 1, 2026.
The move came in a notice sent to customers,
and it applies to every MLCC product under the pricing code the company manages as one group.

Taiyo Yuden is raising MLCC prices from September 1.

@@REF@@MLCC price wave: after Taiyo Yuden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics raises prices 30% from August (TechNews, 2026-07-28)|https://technews.tw/2026/07/28/samsung-electro-mechanics-taiyo-yuden-mlcc-prices-raised/|https://img.technews.tw/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/21113447/samsung.jpg

## What an MLCC is, and why 30% matters

Open up a phone and you find hundreds of parts smaller than a grain of rice sitting on the board.
Most of them are MLCCs.

The part holds a small charge and releases it on demand, smoothing out the voltage,
so that when a chip suddenly draws a burst of current the supply does not sag or spike.

Equipment that draws more power needs more of them.
A high-end AI server carries more than ten times the MLCC count of a smartphone.
Each one is cheap, but the sheer number means a single price step lands directly in the cost of a server.

## How this differs from the last increase

MLCC prices already moved once this spring.
Taiyo Yuden raised prices on some products from May 1, and the reason it gave then was the rising cost of gold and silver.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics, which holds roughly 23% of the global market, stayed put.

@@REF@@Taiyo Yuden to raise prices across passive components from May (SemiMedia, 2026-04-15)|https://www.semimedia.cc/20906.html|https://c.semimedia.cc/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026041501.jpg

That report says the notice reached past MLCCs to inductors, ferrite beads, RF parts and some aluminum electrolytic capacitors.
The reason it gave was rising costs for raw materials including metals, and for production itself, naming metals broadly rather than gold and silver.
Three months later the one that moved first was not the leader Murata but the number two, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and the step was 30%.

The reason it gave is also different from the spring.
Instead of input costs, the company pointed to structural growth in electronics demand putting pressure on the supply chain beyond what it can absorb internally.

If raw materials are the reason, falling input costs eventually give a company grounds to walk the price back.
If demand is the reason, no such grounds exist.

## Delivery dates bind before prices do

Taiyo Yuden paired its increase with a warning that it may not be able to meet the delivery schedules customers request.
That is the company saying supply will fall short of demand even after the price goes up.

Prices can be negotiated. Delivery dates cannot.
It also means the thing keeping a server from shipping on time may not be a GPU but a component smaller than a fingernail.

## So what actually settles this

It comes down to one question.
Does the 30% harden into real contract prices, or does it stay a notice.

If August shipments bill at the new prices and Murata joins the round of increases,
pricing power has moved from the buyers of these parts to the makers of them.
If customers instead delay orders or shift volume elsewhere and the increase sticks only on part of the lineup,
the notice will have been a negotiating card.

The heavier line is not the one about raising prices. It is the one about not being able to supply enough even at the higher price.
The shortage the AI buildout created appears to have worked its way past GPUs and memory down to the cheapest layer of the bill of materials.

## Why a capacitor is chip news
This part is smaller than a fingernail. It is called a capacitor.
It stores a small burst of electricity and releases it to keep power steady inside a circuit.

A single server board holds thousands of them,
and the ones built by stacking ceramic layers are called MLCCs.

AI servers draw far more power and tolerate far less noise than a regular PC,
so they need many more MLCCs, and better ones.

## What actually happened
TrendForce data cited by Jukan shows June shipments from Murata,
Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Taiyo Yuden hit their highest level in five years.
AI demand is what pushed their production lines there.

@@CHK@@Murata book-to-bill|1.30|Samsung Electro-Mechanics book-to-bill|1.31|Taiyo Yuden book-to-bill|1.25@@The peak during the worst MLCC shortage on record, in 2018, was 1.25. @@REF@@AI demand for high-end MLCCs pushes Japan and Korea suppliers' order backlogs to post-pandemic highs (TrendForce, 2026-07-06)|https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260706-13136.html|https://www.trendforce.com/images/trendforce_og_04.jpg

Prices moved with them.
Distributors who had stocked up ahead of time raised prices 20 to 25%,
and spot prices climbed as much as three times their earlier level.
Inventory on key parts has fallen to 30 days or less.

## Why the shortage hit now
The cause is not demand alone. It is allocation.
Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Taiyo Yuden are shifting lines
that used to make consumer-grade parts (X5R) toward the higher AI-grade spec (X6S, X7R).

A factory cannot double its output overnight,
so a line that gains capacity on one side gives it up on the other.

The parts actually running short are mid-capacity capacitors (1 to 22 microfarads)
used in ordinary appliances and cars.

## Who fills the gap the big three leave
This is the part Jukan's post does not mention.
As the big three chase AI orders,
Taiwan's Yageo and Walsin Technology are stepping into the consumer-grade orders they leave behind.

@@REF@@AI servers trigger an MLCC cannibalization wave, Taiwanese makers stand to benefit (BigGo Finance, 2026-07-06)|https://finance.biggo.com/news/cf5c9f57-9901-4633-ba07-1f9a93d558ac|https://img.biggo.com/QzarOl9HWwK3GCYWo1_-8p8llPF9znpepkRu4YTIZvo/fit/1200/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA3L2NmNWM5ZjU3LTk5MDEtNDYzMy1iYTA3LTFmOWE5M2Q1NThhY18xNzgzMzI5MDMxX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.jpg

A shortage at the top three becomes an order surge for the smaller Taiwanese makers.
The same pattern played out in the 2018 MLCC crunch, when Taiwanese suppliers gained share.

## What settles this
The question comes down to one thing.
Is this a structural bottleneck that rides the AI server boom for several quarters,
or a temporary supply knot that unwinds once inventory rebuilds.

If Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Taiyo Yuden's book-to-bill ratios
stay above 1.25 through Q3 and Q4, the structural read holds.
If the inventory that fell below 30 days returns to normal by year-end, this was a knot, not a wall.

While memory chip prices swing through headlines,
a much smaller and cheaper part is quietly setting the pace of AI hardware production.

## Why this story is back
A Bloomberg-sourced report today could move Korean markets too.
Nvidia is reportedly discussing guaranteeing $250 billion of OpenAI's Ohio data-center debt,
plus up to $350 billion more so OpenAI can buy Nvidia's own chips.

OpenAI is an unprofitable private company with sub-investment-grade credit.
A data-center builder needs its tenant's credit to borrow cheaply from banks,
and Nvidia is filling that gap for OpenAI.

The same dollars move from Nvidia to OpenAI, to Oracle,
and back to Nvidia as chip revenue.
Add Nvidia's stakes in CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN, and this circular financing tops $540 billion.

## The same structure showed up 25 years ago
In the late 1990s, telecom firms raced to lay fiber-optic cable,
betting the internet would make data traffic explode.

Cash-poor startups borrowed from equipment makers to buy that equipment,
and the loans were structured so the money flowed straight back as the lender's own sales.
Nearly $30 billion in such vendor loans went out in 2000 alone.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/BalticServers_data_center.jpg/960px-BalticServers_data_center.jpg|Today's equivalent of the fiber build-out. This is where the money actually goes.|BalticServers.com · CC BY-SA 3.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:BalticServers_data_center.jpg

Then data-compression techniques and DWDM (wavelength-division multiplexing) spread through the market,
and the fiber already in the ground turned out to be more than enough.
One new technology was all it took to pop the bubble.

The Nasdaq, which had peaked at 5,048 in March 2000, fell 78% by 2002,
and $2 trillion of telecom-stock value vanished.
Roughly 95% of the fiber laid at the time was never lit even once.

## Where it differs this time
The fiber bubble was built on demand that was overestimated from the start.
Today's AI data-center demand is, at least so far, backed by real contracts and revenue.

By scale, though, this round is already bigger.
As of 2025, Nvidia's vendor financing equaled 67% of its own revenue,
2.8 times larger relative to revenue than Lucent's vendor loans at the telecom bubble's height.

@@REF@@Circular Financing: Does Nvidia's $110B Bet Echo the Telecom Bubble? (Tomasz Tunguz, 2025-10-03)|https://tomtunguz.com/nvidia_nortel_vendor_financing_comparison/|https://res.cloudinary.com/dzawgnnlr/image/upload/v1/n8ynkgcfy39ny8x4ctue

Relative to revenue, this loop has already passed the dot-com peak,
so the shock could be larger too if the chain ever breaks.

## The weakest link
The weakest part of this structure is OpenAI's own finances.
OpenAI reportedly spends $1.22 for every dollar it earns,
and its IPO-track filings project breaking even only around 2030.

HSBC estimates OpenAI needs at least $207 billion more financing through 2030 to stay afloat.
@@REF@@OpenAI must find $207bn to meet AI data center spending commitments - HSBC (DataCenterDynamics, 2025-11-28)|https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/openai-must-find-207bn-to-meet-ai-data-center-spending-commitments-hsbc/|https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/1024px-Sam_Altman_speaking_at_TED.2e16d0ba.fill-1200x630.jpg

A $25 billion-revenue company would have to carry $80-100 billion a year in compute commitments for five years running.
Nvidia, Oracle and OpenAI are investor, supplier and customer to each other at once,
so trouble at any one can spread like dominoes.
Nvidia's cash generation should keep it standing, but OpenAI and Oracle are first in line.

## What decides this
The question comes down to three things:
can AI make enough money to justify hundreds of billions in infrastructure,
can OpenAI keep raising cash until it does,
and does a more efficient technology arrive that needs fewer GPUs.

If OpenAI keeps raising money and grows into its contracts, this loop ends differently from 25 years ago.
If signs appear it cannot close HSBC's $207 billion gap, the picture changes first.
Last time, a single new technology was enough to make the demand itself disappear.
Whether that happens again decides how long this circular-financing structure survives.

kobeissi-saudi-east-west-pipeline-asia:
Since the Strait of Hormuz closed, Saudi crude bound for Asia crosses the country and leaves from the other coast.
Taking May alone, China loaded about 774,000 barrels a day at that port, South Korea about 645,000, Japan about 452,000 and India about 387,000.
Together the four take about 2.26 million barrels a day, more than half of everything leaving Yanbu.

@@REF@@Original post: The Kobeissi Letter (X, 2026-07-27)|https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2081826308921933996

## Where is Yanbu, and why there

The East-West pipeline runs 746 miles, about 1,200 kilometres, from the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
Crude that leaves from there never enters the Gulf, so it never has to pass through Hormuz.
For South Korea, that means much of its Saudi crude is now loaded on the opposite sea from where it used to come.

Loadings at Yanbu really did jump.
They have run above 4 million barrels a day since June, against 973,000 barrels a day around the same period a year earlier.
In the same report, industry sources say Yanbu has been fixing at maximum capacity for weeks and there is not much room for higher shipments.

@@REF@@Yanbu Port Reaches Near Maximum Crude Shipments (MarineLink, 2026-07-14)|https://www.marinelink.com/news/yanbu-port-reaches-near-maximum-crude-541215|https://images.marinelink.com/images/maritime/w800/adobe-stockphotocreo-172219.jpeg

## So why are the volumes falling

This is where the numbers part ways.
Wood Mackenzie's count has the Red Sea bypass peaking at about 4.07 million barrels a day in March and falling 41% to about 2.39 million by June.
The same data has total Gulf crude exports collapsing 82%, from 18.8 million barrels a day in January to 3.4 million in June.

@@CHK@@Red Sea bypass (March peak)|4.07M b/d|Red Sea bypass (June 2026)|2.39M b/d|Change|-41%@@At the moment this route was described as having become critical, its volumes had been shrinking for four months. A route mattering more and a route carrying more are two different statements.@@2026-07-27 · Wood Mackenzie data (as reported by Hydrocarbon Engineering)

@@CMP@@Kobeissi's reading|The May buyer list shows four Asian countries taking 2.26 million barrels a day from Yanbu. The detour has settled in.|Wood Mackenzie's reading|Volumes routed to the Red Sea fell from 4.07 million in March to 2.39 million in June. The detour is already retreating.

One side counts a single month's buyer list, the other counts four months of flow.
That is why the same port points in two directions.

## Does the detour have a chokepoint of its own

Before it closed, Hormuz carried about 11.4 million barrels a day.
Even at its peak, the Yanbu route moved a little over a third of that.
One pipeline does not stand in for one strait.

Wood Mackenzie's Ian Solis puts it plainly: Yanbu has its own chokepoint.
If Bab al-Mandeb comes under sustained disruption from a declared Houthi naval blockade, Asia stands to lose a major crude supply artery.
Crude loaded at Yanbu still has to pass through that narrow entrance to reach Asia.

@@REF@@Wood Mackenzie: Saudi Arabia's Red Sea crude bypass peaks in March and declines 41% by June (Hydrocarbon Engineering, 2026-07-27)|https://www.hydrocarbonengineering.com/special-reports/27072026/wood-mackenzie-saudi-arabias-red-sea-crude-bypass-peaks-in-march-and-declines-41-by-june/|https://dlgivnpf6gg8w.cloudfront.net/media/articles/pop/oil-drum-02.jpg

## What settles it

The question comes down to one thing.
Is the Yanbu route a replacement for Hormuz, or a buffer that buys time while costs climb?

The place to watch is Bab al-Mandeb.
If traffic through that strait holds, Yanbu looks like a replacement; if the Houthi blockade keeps turning ships around, it ends as a buffer.

For South Korea this is not somebody else's problem.
On May figures it was the second-largest buyer at that port, and the crude still arrives through one narrow entrance.
jukan-asml-selloff-china-duv-pushback:
ASML shares have slid for two straight days, down roughly 12% over the past month.
The trigger was news that China has begun mass-producing its own DUV lithography tools.
Chip analyst Jukan and Bank of America (BofA) both argue the reaction has gone too far.

Shares fell more than 6% on the 27th when the China DUV news broke, then slid another 4% at the open on the 28th, deepening the drop.

## Why isn't this a surprise

Jukan says the news itself isn't particularly shocking.
Most people already had a vague sense this was coming, he argues.

There's a reason for that.
The newly named maker, Shanghai Yuliangsheng, was founded in 2022 by pooling DUV R&D teams from several Chinese firms.
SMIC has been testing its lithography tool since September 2025.
That's ten months before the news broke on the 27th, meaning the program was already deep into validation.

@@REF@@China begins mass-producing homegrown DUV tools (Tom's Hardware, 2026-07-28)|https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/china-begins-mass-production-of-domestic-immersion-duv-lithography-machines|https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/7ZotSVaMnrDA7FNSEBa4BN-970-80.jpg

## How solid is the sourcing, really

Jukan went a step further.
He claims the report actually traces back to remarks a professor at a Chinese Jiaotong university made during an internal meeting.

We couldn't independently confirm that specific detail through other outlets.
Tom's Hardware and other coverage describe the sourcing only as two people familiar with the program.
The manufacturer's name wasn't disclosed at first either, and only surfaced later as Yuliangsheng.
ASML itself declined to comment when asked.
The reporting clearly leans on anonymous sourcing, but exactly whose words are behind it differs by outlet.

@@CMP@@The threat-is-real read|China starting DUV mass production reads as the first real crack in ASML's lithography monopoly.|Jukan and BofA's read|The report leans on two anonymous sources and ASML wouldn't confirm it. Next year's output still caps at 20 units, more a confirmation of an already-known program than new news.
What it comes down to is whether you treat this as fresh news or as confirmation of a program that's been running for ten months already.

## Where is the market actually placing its bets

BofA kept its Buy rating on ASML through the selloff.
Its reasoning: this is a trade-related worry, not a sign anything is wrong with the business.
BofA's 2027-2028 earnings estimates sit 6-7% above Wall Street consensus.
It expects AI-driven wafer fab equipment spending to top $250 billion by 2028.

@@REF@@ASML stock slips again, why BofA remains strongly bullish (Invezz, 2026-07-28)|https://invezz.com/news/2026/07/28/asml-stock-slips-again-why-bofa-remains-strongly-bullish/|https://invezz-wp-media.lon1.digitaloceanspaces.com/2026/07/image-4-1785234707.png

## What settles it
The question comes down to one thing.
Is this a real reassessment of the threat, or an overreaction to thinly sourced news.

The fact that a single report leaning on two anonymous sources knocked nearly 10% off the lithography sector's bellwether in two days says something about how jumpy this market already is.

What will tell the difference is earnings and volume.
If ASML's strong results continue next quarter and China's output doesn't run far ahead of next year's 20-unit plan, this drop goes down as an overreaction.
If volume ramps faster than expected, or Chinese customers start actually pulling orders from ASML, this drop was the start of the real repricing.
